tl;dr paper "proving" golden rice works was done by testin on children without their parents consent and included feeding the children a diet unrealistic for a third world country, meaning they would have been better off then their peers even without the golden rice.

The crops normally suggested aren't anywhere near native to the region, so it's not anywhere near as simple a matter as you make it. Given the average wealth of the farmer that can't afford afford to feed his children much more than rice, you'd be out everything that wouldn't flourish on its own without additional fertilizer or pesticides; you'd have to teach the farmers, not only how to grow the plants that would survive, but how to cook them and integrate them into their meals; there is also almost certainly some of that rice going to market, so the fact that rice paddies aren't good for next to any other crops is going to put already poor peasants into a further bind.

Golden rice, on the other hand, slots right into what they're already doing.
In other words for trivial book-keeping failures, not any lapse in scientific rigour.
